record.paper_title: Optimal Algorithms for Numerical Integration: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let S_d(f)=integral_{D_d} f(x) rho(x) dx be a weighted multivariate integral over an open set D_d subset R^d, and consider randomized cubature rules of the form A_n^omega(f)=sum_{j=1}^n a_j(omega) f(x_j(omega)), possibly with the sample points x_j chosen as iid uniform points in D_d. Does there exist a universal randomized algorithm for this weighted integration problem, meaning a single algorithm family that works across multiple smoothness classes, with error bounds comparable to those known in the unweighted cube case, perhaps allowing additional logarithmic factors if exact optimal rates are too expensive in practice?

evidence.quote: Study the approximation of the integral Sd(f) = \u222b_Dd f(x)\u03c1(x) dx over an open subset Dd \u2282 Rd for integrable functions f : Dd -> R. We are interested in universal randomized algorithms (A\u03c9n) of the form A\u03c9n(f) = \u2211_{j=1}^n aj(\u03c9)f(xj(\u03c9)), possibly based on iid uniformly distributed xj.

Ideally, we would like to have the same optimal error bounds as in Theorem 3. It is not clear whether such algorithms exist, we know it only for \u03c1 = 1 on Dd = [0,1]d. In addition, the optimal order of convergence may be useless if the involved constants are huge. It might be more practical to relax the order of the error bounds and to allow additional log factors.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D_d \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be an open set, and let $\rho : D_d \to [0,\infty)$ be a fixed integrable weight function such that $\int_{D_d}\rho(x)\,dx < \infty$. For an integrable function $f : D_d \to \mathbb{R}$, define the weighted integral
$$S_d(f) = \int_{D_d} f(x)\,\rho(x)\,dx.$$
A randomized cubature rule using $n$ function values has the form
$$A_n^\omega(f) = \sum_{j=1}^n a_j(\omega)\, f(x_j(\omega)),$$
where $\omega$ is a random element of some probability space, the coefficients $a_j(\omega) \in \mathbb{R}$ and the nodes $x_j(\omega) \in D_d$ are random, and we additionally allow the variant in which $x_1(\omega),\dots,x_n(\omega)$ are i.i.d. uniformly distributed in $D_d$ (assuming $D_d$ has finite Lebesgue measure). The randomized error of $A_n^\omega$ on a class $F$ of integrands is
$$e^{\mathrm{ran}}(A_n^\omega, F) = \sup_{f \in F} \left( \mathbb{E}_\omega \,|S_d(f) - A_n^\omega(f)|^2 \right)^{1/2}.$$

Call a family $(A_n^\omega)_{n \ge 1}$ *universal* if it is defined independently of the smoothness parameters of $F$ and yet, for every class $F$ in a prescribed scale of smoothness classes on $D_d$ (for instance, isotropic or mixed-smoothness Sobolev or Hölder classes), the error $e^{\mathrm{ran}}(A_n^\omega, F)$ satisfies, up to absolute constants and possibly logarithmic factors in $n$, the optimal rate known for randomized integration of $F$ on the unit cube with weight $\rho \equiv 1$.

Question: Does such a universal randomized algorithm exist for the weighted integration problem $S_d$ on a general open set $D_d \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with a general integrable weight $\rho$, achieving for every smoothness class in the scale the optimal randomized rate up to (at worst) additional polylogarithmic factors in $n$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the area of optimal randomized algorithms for numerical integration. Universal randomized algorithms with near-optimal rates are known for the unweighted case $\rho=1$ on $[0,1]^d$, but no analogous construction appears to be known for general weighted integration on general domains $D_d$. No publication establishing such universal algorithms in the general weighted setting was found.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Algorithms for Numerical Integration: Recent Results and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discusses optimal randomized integration and lists universal algorithms for weighted integration as an open problem; the unweighted cube case is the only one known.
status_evidence.claim: Universality of randomized cubature for weighted integrals on general domains is stated as open, with only $\rho=1$ on $[0,1]^d$ resolved.
